analysis.title: GS - Milhous - CAS Mark to Market for Thursday - 29 Oct 2026
key_insights: US equities finished mixed on Thursday 10/29: SPX -30 bps to 7720, NDX -138 bps to 28,402, RTY +101 bps to 2859. The equal-weight index outperformed the cap-weighted benchmark by 150 bps, led by rate-sensitive sectors.

Sector dispersion was wide: Healthcare +2.50%, Real Estate +2.25%, Consumer Staples +1.64%, Utilities +1.56% and Financials +1.52% led, while Communication Services -6.60%, Tech -0.88% and Consumer Discretionary -0.63% lagged. 8 of 11 sectors finished higher.
Mega-cap tech fell on disappointing earnings. After the bell AMZN fell 5% on weaker AWS growth, and NOW dropped 26.96% after a weak Q3 report.
Consumer names caught a bid on rotation out of tech, and the GS Discretionary basket (GSXUCOND) finished +3.29%.
US rates rallied sharply into the close on the tech earnings weakness. 1y1y rate -17bps, 2y notes -10bps, 10y notes -8bps and 30y bonds -4.5bps in yield terms (described as richer).
Core PCE came in line with consensus and Q3 GDP was stronger than expected. The December FOMC meeting has 18.5bps of hikes priced.
The ECB left rates unchanged and front-end European government bonds rallied on the dovish statement. The $44b 7y auction was a nonevent, stopping on the screws.
Macro credit went out notably wider: CDX IG +1.35bps wider and CDX HY -27cts lower. Credit lagged broad equity indices after outperforming earlier in the week.

Credit tone soured late after AMZN and INTC earnings. 5y CDS widened 20 in both SPCX and INTC, CRWV slid another 1pt after hyperscaler earnings, and HY healthcare names fell after poor numbers from CYH.
Primary credit markets priced $36.8bn across 6 deals, led by MSFT's $25bn 10-tranche jumbo deal.

FX: The Dollar reversed an early bid as US yields fell. EUR recovered from YTD lows (+25bps) after Lagarde's language was less dovish than expected and signaled a December hike, despite an initial -25bps drop post-ECB hold.

Risk-off FX tone lifted CHF +45bps, with AUD the only underperformer at -35bps. USDJPY was roughly flat ahead of the BOJ decision, with some safe-haven support from the tech selloff and lower US front-end yields.

Tomorrow's calendar is lighter into month end: Q3 ECI at 8:30am (GS +0.8%, consensus +0.8%, last +0.9%), Oct Chicago PMI, Fed speakers Daly (12pm) and Musalem (12:30pm), a BoJ decision overnight, and a batch of euro area GDP and HICP flashes.

market_movers.rationale: NOW dropped 26.96% after a weak Q3 earnings report, per the note's equity summary.
AMZN fell 5% post-bell after reporting weaker AWS growth.
Disappointing INTC earnings contributed to a 20 bp widening in its 5y CDS.
CRWV credit slid another 1pt after hyperscaler earnings.
Poor CYH numbers sent HY healthcare names sharply lower.

earnings_insights: NOW: reported Q3 results described as weak, stock -26.96% (reported Thursday 10/29, after the bell).
AMZN: reported Q3 results with weaker AWS growth, stock -5% post-bell (reported 10/29). No figures given.
INTC: earnings described as disappointing (reported 10/29), 5y CDS +20.
CYH: poor reported numbers (10/29) weighed on HY healthcare names.
Tomorrow's Q3 Employment Cost Index forecast is GS +0.8%, consensus +0.8%, last +0.9%. This is a macro estimate, not an earnings figure.

macro_indicators.interpretation: No surprise from the inflation print, so the rates rally came from tech earnings weakness rather than inflation data.
Growth beat did not stop the rates rally into the close.
Markets price a meaningful chance of a December hike.
Goldman's estimate matches consensus, with the prior quarter at +0.9%.
Consensus is in line with GS, so a print near 0.8% is expected.

risk_factors: Further hyperscaler and tech earnings disappointments could spread to credit, as seen in INTC, SPCX, CRWV and CYH.
Credit lagging equities after earlier outperformance.
A hawkish ECB (December hike signaled) and 18.5bps of Fed hikes priced for December leave rates sensitive.
BoJ decision overnight is a risk for USDJPY.
vol_and_positioning: In credit vol, fast money bought OTM HY downside and sold HY calendar.
A persistent short cover bid took credit index tighter in the morning. EM and macro short covering supported HY, while IG flows were mixed.
Credit saw slight decompressionary flows, with CDX HY down 27cts.
